rationale: Among 1,429 older Australian women, adjusted HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.99–1.04, p=.345) for first fall hospitalization per 20 g/day oranges and other citrus. The 1,468-person Blekkenhorst companion shares the CAIFOS family and found an adjusted HR 1.01 (0.97–1.04) for all fracture hospitalizations. Both lack an orange-only, recurrent-falls or diagnosed Parkinson estimate.

Altemor pilot reports a lower Hunova Silver fall-risk score with a combined supplement and routine-care comparator in older adults. Neither the complete numeric tables nor a separate comparison for event counts, raw orange or Parkinson disease were recovered.

Low combined fruit and vegetable intake was associated with more reported injurious falls (adjusted OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.05–1.90). A cross-sectional survey of dietary groups cannot transfer that direction to raw orange in Parkinson disease.

The dried Citrus unshiu peel belongs to a multi-herb formulation in an uncontrolled dementia with Lewy bodies sleep trial. The specific safety inquiry found no falls linked to sedation or muscle relaxation. It does not measure all-cause fall frequency.
The Parkinson protocol plans prospective falls safety capture under diet and exercise arms. Target enrollment is 80, no results are posted, and no isolated raw-orange comparison is included.
